source_pins.finding: Appsink uses an explicitly bounded queue; max-buffers/max-time/max-bytes limit accumulation, leaky-type selects drop behavior, and current releases expose in/out/dropped counters. Blocking a streaming producer is explicitly called out as harmful to realtime behavior.

Append-only consistency and inclusion can be cryptographically proven with Merkle/compact-range structures, but this requires additional retained tree/proof material; consistency proofs are logarithmic rather than constant-state complete-history proofs.
Merkle consistency proofs establish that a later log state is an append-only extension of an earlier state and enable efficient detection of inconsistent views.

BLAKE3 supports incremental hashing and efficient cumulative commitments, but incremental hashing alone does not supply arbitrary historical inclusion or append-only consistency proofs without retained auxiliary structure.

f2_observation.current_mechanism: bounded frame-ref ring + exact total drop count + bounded recent dropped IDs + origin provenance + prior-state SHA-256 + current-frame SHA-256
f2_observation.current_property: O(capacity) live state with O(1) rolling predecessor commitment beyond the bounded ring
f2_observation.important_boundary: The current rolling predecessor digest is a cumulative commitment. By itself, when prior states are discarded, it is not an independently replayable complete-history log or an inclusion-proof system. Full audit requires external retained checkpoints/states/receipts.

result: The current F2 broker architecture is already aligned with mature realtime bounded-queue practice. Importing a transparency-log/Merkle framework into the broker would violate the current thin bounded-state design for little immediate gain. The useful external lesson is semantic: keep the broker's rolling hash as a compact cumulative commitment and place any stronger long-history verification in a separate persisted audit/checkpoint layer rather than inside the realtime broker.
counterhypothesis: If future F2 acceptance requires cryptographic inclusion/consistency proofs for arbitrary historical frame-reference events without trusting stored prior broker states, a Merkle compact-range/transparency-log layer may become justified outside the broker.
next_discriminator: Map whether an existing F2 persistent receipt/journal surface can checkpoint broker generation + broker SHA-256 cheaply; if yes, distill an explicit checkpoint contract rather than importing Merkle/BLAKE3 dependencies.
